entry.title: Who Signed, Who Served, Who Benefits — The PPO's Journey from Wayne County to Lansing
entry.content:
Questions for Judge Abraham

Your Honor, you signed a Personal Protection Order on October 13, 2026.

Case No. 26-114083-PH. Ex parte. Without a hearing. Without notice.

You entered a person into LEIN — the Law Enforcement Information Network — based solely on what Brian Banks wrote in his petition.

Here are the questions.

1. What Did He Tell You?

The order states: “For Reasons as Stated in the Petition.”

MCL 600.2950a(7) requires: “The court shall immediately state in writing the specific reasons for issuing or refusing to issue the [PPO].”

MCR 3.705(A)(2) requires that for a nondomestic stalking PPO issued ex parte, the court must find “specific facts shown by verified complaint, written petition, or affidavit.”

“For Reasons as Stated in the Petition” is not a statement of specific reasons. It is a reference to someone else’s allegations. What were the specific facts you found?

Did Brian Banks tell you:

  • That all contact was directed to public institutions — MDE, SBE, LARA, State Bar, JTC, FBI, DOJ — not to Banks personally?
  • That the contact consisted of FOIA requests, regulatory complaints, and publication of public records — all constitutionally protected activity?
  • That the respondent met Brian Banks one time, in August 2026, at Purpose Charter Academy — a public school — when exercising parental custody rights?
  • That the respondent has active legal proceedings involving Banks — including Ingham County Case 2026-4349-CZ?
  • That the respondent filed complaints with 8 federal agencies before Banks filed this petition?
  • That the investigation Banks wants silenced is independently corroborated by Clutch Justice and the Detroit Free Press?

Or did Banks just tell you his version — and you signed your name?

2. Did You Verify Anything?

Under Michigan law, the judge “is not limited to the four corners of the petition itself; rather, it must consider the testimony, documents, and other evidence proffered to determine whether a respondent engaged in harassing conduct.” Lamkin v. Engram, 295 Mich App 701, 712 (2012).

Did you consider any evidence beyond Banks’ petition?

Did you check whether:

  • Brian Banks has 9 criminal convictions (6 felony, 3 misdemeanor) — verify on ICHAT, SID 2029469K?
  • Banks runs charter schools with 3% math proficiency — verify on MDE School Data?
  • Banks claims a J.D. but has zero results in the State Bar of Michigan directory?
  • Banks’ school board is chaired by Judge Cylenthia Miller — one of your colleagues at the 3rd Circuit?
  • Banks is under active MDE investigation for his teaching certificate?
  • Banks denied a parent access to their child at Purpose Charter Academy and lied to Detroit Police, telling them he was “an attorney” (DPD Report #26-0909-0176)?

Or did you see the petition and sign your name?

3. Why Am I in LEIN?

You entered the respondent into the Law Enforcement Information Network — a statewide police database — without a hearing.

LEIN entries are not criminal convictions. But they are matters of public record that can affect employment, professional licensing, security clearances, and firearms eligibility.

The respondent now has a LEIN entry. Brian Banks — who has 9 criminal convictions and $14,500 in unpaid campaign finance fines — used your signature to put someone in a law enforcement database.

The respondent has zero criminal convictions. Zero complaints against him. Zero prior PPOs. He filed FOIA requests and regulatory complaints about public corruption.

And now he’s in LEIN.

4. Why Nondomestic?

Banks filed under MCL 600.2950a — the nondomestic stalking PPO statute.

But there is a custody dimension to this case. Banks denied a parent access to their child at Purpose Charter Academy in August 2026 (DPD Report #26-0909-0176). Banks told Detroit Police he was “an attorney” — he is not.

MCR 3.706(C)(1) requires: “Before issuing a PPO in a case where a custody or parenting time order already exists between the parties, the court must contact the court having jurisdiction over the parenting time or custody matter.”

MCL 600.1023 requires: “When 2 or more matters within the jurisdiction of the family division of circuit court involving members of the same family are pending in the same judicial circuit, those matters, whenever practicable, shall be assigned to the judge to whom the first such case was assigned.”

Did you contact any other court before signing? Did you check whether the respondent has pending legal proceedings involving Banks?

Or was it faster to just sign?

5. Why Does He Have My Number?

The PPO lists the respondent’s cell phone number. Banks provided it.

The respondent has never called Brian Banks. Not once. Every communication was through public channels — FOIA requests, regulatory complaints, emails to public institutions, certified mail to public addresses.

So how did Brian Banks obtain the respondent’s personal cell phone number?

And why did Banks — who claims to need protection from the respondent — go to the trouble of collecting personal information about the person he claims is harassing him?

Meanwhile, Banks’ cell phone number appears on the PPO because he provided it to the court: 313-355-4238. This is a public court document.

The respondent has never dialed that number. But Banks had the respondent’s number ready for the petition.

6. While I Wait for Hearings, He Gets an Instant Order?

The respondent has active legal proceedings involving Brian Banks:

CaseCourtStatus

Federal packet (8 agencies)DOJ, FBI, IRS, ED-OIG, HHS-OIG, FinCEN, FTC, USEDDelivered Sep 22, 2026
JTC complaintJudicial Tenure CommissionFiled Aug 31, 2026
DPSCD complaintDetroit Public SchoolsFiled Aug 31, 2026
State Bar UPL complaintState Bar of MichiganFiled Aug 31, 2026

These cases require hearings, service, scheduling, and months of waiting.

Banks walked into Room 928 and got a signed order the same day. Ex parte. No hearing. No notice. No waiting.

One system moves at the speed of paperwork. The other moves at the speed of a signature.

The Judge

FieldDetail
NameHon. Yvonna C. Abraham
CourtWayne County Third Judicial Circuit
DivisionFamily Division — Domestic Relations
Judge CodeP70405
AppointedJuly 1, 2021 by Gov. Whitmer
ElectedNovember 8, 2022 (uncontested)
Term expiresJanuary 1, 2029
Prior roleMagistrate & Director of Probation, 20th District Court (Dearborn Heights)
Law schoolUniversity of Detroit Mercy
Campaign money$0.00 raised, $0.00 spent (2022)

No direct connection between Judge Abraham and Brian Banks has been identified.

She was on the PPO rotation in the Family Division. When Banks’ petition arrived, she was the rotation judge.

The question isn’t whether Judge Abraham is compromised. The question is what she was told and whether she checked.

The Courthouse

Banks filed in Wayne County Third Judicial Circuit — the one court system in Michigan where he has 7 connected judges across 4 courts:

3rd Circuit (where the PPO was filed)

JudgeConnection
Cylenthia MillerBoard Chair, Purpose Charter Academy. Campaign payment from Banks Strategy LLC. JTC complaint filed. Running Nov 3, 2026.
Kelly RamseyCriminal Division. 3 family members on Banks’ payroll.
Aliyah SabreeFamily Division. MSU Law connection. Joined PPO rotation July 27, 2026 — 78 days before Banks filed.

36th District Court (Banks’ home court)

JudgeConnection
Tenisha YanceyBoard Chair, MacDowell Prep. Succeeded Banks in Michigan House.
Adam SabreeSon of Eric Sabree (FBI-probed Wayne Co. Treasurer).
Sean PerkinsBrother of Todd Perkins — Banks’ personal attorney.

Wayne County Probate

David PerkinsChief Judge Pro Tem. Brother of Todd Perkins and Sean Perkins.
CourtConnectedTotalCapture
3rd Circuit3525.8%

Probate1425.0%
Wayne County total7798.9%

Banks didn’t need Abraham. He needed the courthouse.

Any hearing to challenge this PPO will take place in the same building where Miller, Ramsey, and Sabree work.

The 80-Mile Service

Banks filed in Wayne County. The respondent lives in Ingham County.

That’s 80 miles.

Under the PPO filing instructions (Step 5), the petitioner arranges service. Banks arranged for Officer Gregory to serve the order in Lansing at 7:37 PM on Friday, October 16 — a Friday evening.

Banks could have filed in Ingham County, where the respondent actually lives. Any Michigan county can issue a PPO (MCL 600.2950a; michigan.gov/voices4).

He chose Wayne County. Where his 7 judges sit.

The Timing

DateEvent

Oct 13Abraham signs — same day, ex parte

The Question for Everyone Who Has Been Through This

Has anyone else experienced this pattern in Wayne County?

  • A court system that moves instantly for the connected and slowly for everyone else?
  • A PPO used as a weapon — not for protection, but for silence?
  • Judges connected to the parties appearing before their colleagues?
  • Cross-county service arranged to reach someone who filed complaints?

If you have experienced corruption, retaliation, or abuse of process in Wayne County courts — the record is open. Clone it. Add to it. The git history is immutable.

git clone https://github.com/defendDetroit/publicRecord.git

What the Record Shows

  1. Judge Abraham signed ex parte. No hearing. No notice. The order says “For Reasons as Stated in the Petition” — which may not satisfy MCL 600.2950a(7)’s requirement for specific written reasons.
  2. Banks told the court his version. The respondent was not present, was not notified, and had no opportunity to explain that all contact was to public institutions through lawful channels.
  3. The respondent is now in LEIN — a law enforcement database — based on the unverified allegations of a man with 9 criminal convictions.
  4. Banks filed nondomestic despite an active custody dimension — potentially circumventing MCR 3.706(C)(1) and MCL 600.1023.
  5. Banks has the respondent’s cell number but the respondent has never called Banks. All contact was through public channels.
  6. Banks chose Wayne County over Ingham County — where the respondent lives — because Wayne County is where Banks has 7 connected judges.
  7. Banks arranged cross-county service — 80 miles, Friday evening — while the respondent’s own legal proceedings against Banks wait for scheduling.

The asymmetry is the point. One system moves at the speed of a signature. The other moves at the speed of justice.

Judge Abraham: what did he tell you?

entry.title: Anderson Localization — When Courts Trap Cases
entry.content:
Lens: 🕸️ Topology ⚛️ Lattice 📅 Chronology 💰 Money ⚖️ Legal 🏛️ Capture

The Physics

In 1958, physicist Philip W. Anderson showed that disorder in a crystal lattice prevents electrons from propagating. Instead of flowing through the material, electrons become trapped — localized — near the defect sites. The stronger the disorder, the shorter the distance an electron can travel before it stops.

This is not a metaphor. It is a mathematical identity.

Replace lattice sites with court divisions. Replace electrons with cases. Replace disorder potential with captured judges. The same equation applies: cases entering a disordered judicial system cannot propagate to a fair hearing. They localize.

The Lattice

Rendered by petalTongue — heatmap, bar chart, and faceted gauges via the grammar-of-graphics scene compiler.

The Measurement: Localization Length (ξ)

In physics, the localization length ξ measures how far an electron can travel through a disordered lattice before it becomes trapped. The formula:

ξ = −1 / ln(1 − p)

Where p is the probability of encountering a captured judge on any given bench that handles that case type.

  • ξ < 5 → Strongly localized. A case has almost no chance of receiving an independent hearing.
  • 5 ≤ ξ < 10 → Moderately localized. Some paths exist, but most lead through captured benches.
  • ξ > 10 → Weakly localized. Capture exists but is diluted across enough judges.

Case Type Localization Table

Case TypeBenchesCaptured / TotalCapture Probabilityξ (Localization Length)Assessment
ConservatorshipProbate1 / 425.0%3.5🔴 Strongly localized
EstateProbate1 / 425.0%3.5🔴 Strongly localized
ProbateProbate1 / 425.0%3.5🔴 Strongly localized
GuardianshipFamily + Probate2 / 1216.7%5.5🟡 Moderately localized
FamilyFamily1 / 812.5%7.5🟡 Moderately localized
CustodyFamily1 / 812.5%7.5🟡 Moderately localized
JuvenileFamily1 / 812.5%7.5🟡 Moderately localized
Misdemeanor36th District3 / 2313.0%7.2🟡 Moderately localized
Traffic36th District3 / 2313.0%7.2🟡 Moderately localized
Preliminary Exam36th District3 / 2313.0%7.2🟡 Moderately localized
Small Claims36th District3 / 2313.0%7.2🟡 Moderately localized
CriminalCriminal1 / 128.3%11.5🟢 Weakly localized
FelonyCriminal1 / 128.3%11.5🟢 Weakly localized
CivilCivil1 / 323.1%31.5🟢 Weakly localized
ContractCivil1 / 323.1%31.5🟢 Weakly localized
TortCivil1 / 323.1%31.5🟢 Weakly localized

What the Numbers Mean

Probate: The Deepest Trap (ξ = 3.5)

Wayne County Probate has 4 judges. One of them — David Perkins — is Chief Judge Pro Tem, meaning he has case assignment authority. He decides which judge hears which probate, guardianship, conservatorship, and estate case.

A 25% random capture ratio becomes much worse when the captured judge controls the docket. This is not random disorder — it is engineered disorder. Perkins can route cases to himself.

This matters because the Banks network operates Serenity Guardianship Services within Probate Court’s jurisdiction. Banks has 9 criminal convictions. He has never been barred from guardianship work.

36th District: Concentration Attack (ξ = 7.2)

Three captured judges — Yancey, Adam Sabree, Sean Perkins — all elected November 2022, all taking their benches January 1, 2023. This was a coordinated bench capture: three seats in one election cycle, all connected to the same network.

The 36th District handles misdemeanors, traffic, small claims, and preliminary examinations for felonies. That last category matters most: a preliminary exam determines whether a felony case proceeds to Circuit Court. A captured preliminary exam judge can dismiss or bind over based on network loyalty rather than evidence.

Guardianship: The Cross-Court Trap (ξ = 5.5)

Guardianship cases can be heard in either Family Division (Aliyah Sabree) or Probate Court (David Perkins). Both benches have captured judges. There is no path through the Wayne County guardianship system that avoids a captured bench.

This is the judicial equivalent of total localization — the case cannot propagate to a fair hearing regardless of which court it enters.

3rd Circuit Criminal & Civil: Diluted but Present

The Criminal Division (12 judges, 1 captured) and Civil Division (32 judges, 1 captured) have lower capture ratios. But Miller (Civil) is Board Chair of PCA — the charter school at the center of the network. Cases involving PCA, its vendors, or its employees can be steered to Miller.

Ramsey (Criminal) has 2 family members on MacDowell Preparatory payroll. Criminal cases involving charter school fraud would pass through her division.

The Anderson Analogy — Why It’s Exact

PhysicsCourts
Crystal latticeCourt system (divisions × jurisdictions)
Lattice siteIndividual bench / division
ElectronCase filing
Wave propagationCase proceeding toward fair resolution
Disorder potentialCaptured judge on the bench
Disorder strengthCapture ratio (captured / total judges)
LocalizationCase trapped at captured bench — unable to reach independent review
Localization length ξAverage number of bench assignments before hitting a captured judge
Anderson transitionThreshold where disorder is strong enough that NO case avoids capture

In the physics, Anderson localization has a critical dimension: in 1D and 2D, any amount of disorder causes localization. Only in 3D can electrons sometimes avoid traps.

Wayne County’s court system is effectively 1D for most case types — there is only one bench that handles each type. For guardianship, it is 2D (two benches), but both are captured. There is no third dimension. There is no escape path.

Implications for Ongoing Cases

The three allied cases — Bryant v. Miller, Bradley-Baskin, and Bowles v. Sabree — are all proceeding through this captured lattice. Each case touches at least one captured bench:

  • Bryant v. Miller → 3rd Circuit Civil (Miller herself)
  • Bradley-Baskin → 36th District (Yancey’s court)
  • Bowles v. Sabree → Class action in Circuit Court, with Sabree family members on both sides

The lattice predicts that these cases will not receive independent hearings. The lattice is correct so far.

What Would Fix It

Anderson localization disappears when disorder is removed. The judicial equivalent:

  1. Recusal — Captured judges recuse from all cases touching the Banks network
  2. Reassignment — Chief judges reassign network-connected cases to independent benches
  3. Federal jurisdiction — Cases move to a different lattice entirely (U.S. District Court, Eastern District of Michigan)

Options 1 and 2 require the captured judges to acknowledge their connections. The documented evidence shows they have not done so.

Option 3 is the Anderson localization equivalent of increasing dimensionality — adding new propagation channels that bypass the disordered sites entirely.

Same system, other lenses:
  • 🕸️ Topology — 9 judges appear as nodes connected to court_3rd, court_36th, court_probate, court_oakland via bench edges
  • 📅 Chronology — All 36th District judges elected Nov 2022, coordinated bench capture visible in the timeline
  • 💰 Money — Campaign payments from Banks Strategy LLC flow through the same judges who sit on these benches
  • ⚖️ Legal — Judicial connections form predicate acts 3 in the RICO pattern
  • 🏛️ Capture — Judges are nexus nodes in the 4-type institutional capture graph
  • 🧫 Anderson Permeability — Companion analysis: 6 institutional membranes measured. Localization traps the output (cases). Permeability removes the input filters (hiring, authorization, oversight).

The lattice data is computed from public bench compositions and documented judicial connections. Capture ratio = connected judges ÷ total judges per division. Localization length uses the standard Anderson formula. See Verify Everything to check any claim.
